choice: figure-it-out with Feature steps; one owner, no helpers
why: three files on one read seam; the 60-minute wall clock left no room for a delegate round trip

choice: the two read seams on LivePollSource: _run_gh_read and _linear_request
why: every gh GET in feed (via the feeder client, now on _adapter_runner) and tracked-read, and every Linear request, already passes through them

choice: 30 s per read including gh retries and backoff; Linear transport run on a daemon thread cut at 30 s
why: urllib's timeout is per socket operation, so a trickling Linear reply had no total cap; gh retries summed to 66 s

choice: a service (github or linear) is skipped for the rest of the cycle after 2 timed-out reads; begin_cycle clears it
why: 2 x 30 s keeps a hung service at 60 s per cycle (ac-2) while one slow endpoint alone does not starve the other tickets (kept test_gh_timeout_on_one_ref_records_it_and_the_cycle_continues)
a gh hang is a network or GitHub outage in the logged cases; per-repo keys would multiply the bound by the repo count

choice: time each read at the seam with the cycle clock's own wall clock, filed under the open phase; dropped the per-ticket timer
why: per-ticket timing only covered tracked-read and used time.monotonic against the phases' time.time; seam timing names feed reads too and cannot double count

choice: warning_sink line once per skipped service per cycle; each skipped read is a poll_errors row as before
why: ticket asks for the skip to be logged

choice: an inline GraphQL query (no mutation, no --input, no @file) takes the bounded read path
why: round-1 f-1: the feeder's blocker-status queries took the 60 s write path past the hang skip; mutations still run once at the write timeout

choice: post_json shuts its sockets at a whole-request deadline; at most 2 Linear calls may still be running, else the request is skipped
why: round-1 f-2: an abandoned thread kept its trickling socket open, so cycles piled up threads and descriptors; the cap covers injected transports and DNS stalls the shutdown cannot reach

choice: the cutoff tracks each socket when it is created and the TLS socket before its handshake
why: round-2 f-2: a proxy CONNECT ran before connect() returned, so a trickling proxy kept its socket and worker past the deadline

choice: the transport deadline is up to 1 s (a quarter of the deadline at most) before the caller deadline
why: round-2 f-2: a cut-off worker frees its slot before the caller gives up, so expired reads do not fill the cap and the next cycle reads; the caller bound stays at the read deadline
